source_spans.locator: Nature 401, published p.584, Abstract: superimposed face/house stimuli with one object moving and task varied across object/attribute
Nature 401, published pp.584-586, experiment and ROI logic: category- and motion-sensitive regions measure attended and unattended attributes
Nature 401, published p.586, control analysis: task-irrelevant attribute of the attended object evokes greater response than same attribute on unattended object

institutions: MIT Department of Brain and Cognitive Sciences

conditions: two transparently superimposed visual objects, one moving and one stationary, with task cue selecting an attribute or object
task: monitor one cued visual attribute while category and motion signals are measured

nodes.description: grouping of category identity and motion into each of two superimposed perceptual objects
task-cued visual attribute that participants monitor
task-irrelevant attribute belonging to the same perceptual object as the selected attribute
corresponding task-irrelevant attribute belonging to the other superimposed object
magnetic-resonance response in category- or motion-sensitive cortical regions
functional imaging readout across task conditions that independently vary selected attribute and which object moves
successful monitoring of the currently cued attribute during each block

relations.description: regional response reflects not only the selected attribute but also the object grouping to which that attribute belongs
an unselected attribute elicits a larger response when it belongs to the selected object than when it belongs to the unselected object
the imaging probe exposes selection effects separately in category- and motion-sensitive regions
the manipulation is tied to successful monitoring of the cued visual attribute
